content:
Translate so \(x_1=0\), and write
\[
a=x_2,\ b=x_3,\ c=x_4,\ d=x_5,\ e=x_6
\]
so \(0<a<b<c<d<e\).

Since \(a+b+c=s_{11}\), exactly \(9\) sums exceed it. The nine sums
\[
a+b+d,\ a+b+e,\ a+c+d,\ a+c+e,\ a+d+e,\ b+c+d,\ b+c+e,\ b+d+e,\ c+d+e
\]
are all \(>a+b+c\). Hence every other sum is \(<a+b+c\), in particular
\[
T=a+e<a+b+c.
\]

Since \(a+b+e=s_{15}\), exactly \(5\) sums exceed it. The five sums
\[
a+c+e,\ a+d+e,\ b+c+e,\ b+d+e,\ c+d+e
\]
are all \(>a+b+e\). Thus every other sum is \(<a+b+e\), especially
\[
b+c+d<a+b+e,
\]
so
\[
c+d<a+e=T.
\]

Now the ten sums below \(a+b+c\) are
\[
a+b,\ a+c,\ a+d,\ a+e,\ b+c,\ b+d,\ b+e,\ c+d,\ c+e,\ d+e.
\]
For \(T=a+e\), we have
\[
a+b<a+c<a+d<T,
\]
and since \(c+d<T\),
\[
b+c<c+d<T,\qquad b+d<c+d<T.
\]
Also
\[
T=a+e<b+e<c+e<d+e.
\]
Thus exactly six of these ten sums are less than \(T\), so \(T\) is the \(7\)th of them. Since all these ten sums are below \(s_{11}\), we get
\[
T=s_7.
\]
Therefore \(m=7\).

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
